instruction: Navigate to chrome://extensions and manually load the unpacked extension located in the helloExtension folder on the Desktop.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.explanation: More detailed instruction specifying to navigate to chrome://extensions page. Verifies the extension path appears in Chrome's installed extensions.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is semantically correct: get_find_unpacked_extension_path reads Chrome Preferences file (~/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences) to extract all installed extension paths from extensions.settings[id].path
Metric logic correctly checks if expected path exists in the list of installed extensions using is_in_list (general.py:76-81)
Complete coverage: evaluator fully verifies the instruction requirement that the unpacked extension was loaded to chrome://extensions
Data flow is semantically correct: getter returns list[str] of extension paths, metric checks if '/home/user/Desktop/helloExtension' is in result list

No postconfig needed: getter reads persistent Preferences file (not transient UI state). Extension installation persists in file even after chrome://extensions page is closed. Static warning is false positive from heuristic.
Robust implementation: getter has good error handling (returns empty list on failure with error logging at chrome.py:1434)
Expected value is semantically correct: /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension matches the helloExtension folder on Desktop mentioned in instruction
Practical execution verified: Chrome Preferences file persists extension data, getter can successfully read this data to verify task completion
